title: Second moment decomposition
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $d,e$ be real-valued functions on the sign cube of dimension $n$, and let $f$ be a real-valued function on the sign cube of dimension $n+1$. Suppose that for every sign $b$ and every point $x$ in the dimension-$n$ cube, $f(b,x)=b\,d(x)+e(x)$, where a sign is viewed as the real number $-1$ or $1$. Then, with expectations taken uniformly over the respective sign cubes, $\mathbb{E}[f^2]=\mathbb{E}[d^2]+\mathbb{E}[e^2]$.
hypotheses_covered: $d,e$ are real-valued functions on the dimension-$n$ sign cube
$f$ is a real-valued function on the dimension-$(n+1)$ sign cube
